items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The small change to Prefetch.__init__ is clear. The nested if splits the existing raw/values check from the new `if queryset.query.is_sliced:` check, the formatting matches the surrounding code and the error message is plain.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The structure is clean, but the fix sits in the wrong layer. It adds a guard in Prefetch.__init__ when the change belonged in related_descriptors get_prefetch_queryset. The new check blocks a valid use case the hidden tests expect to work.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It validates input at the boundary with `raise ValueError("Cannot prefetch_related a sliced queryset.")` and swallows no errors. But it rejects valid input instead of handling it, so the user's case still fails, only with a different error.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: It never applies any per-parent slice. Sliced querysets are rejected outright, and there is no Window/RowNumber partitioning, no clear_limits and no handling of open or bounded slices. Hidden tests: F2P 0/4 (PrefetchLimitTests all fail).
